easy.def: To take hold of something fast.
examples: Grab my hand.
He grabbed the ball.
I grabbed my coat.

more.def: To take hold of something quickly and firmly.
examples: She grabbed the rope and pulled herself up.
Grab your coat because it is cold out.
The bear grabbed a fish out of the stream.
I am in third grade.
She is in fifth grade.
My brother is in first grade.

more.def: A level or year in school.
examples: I am in the third grade.
My sister is in fifth grade.
Our school has grades one through five.
I got a good grade.
He got an A grade.
Her grade was high.

more.def: A letter or number that shows how well you did.
examples: She got a good grade on the spelling test.
He worked hard to raise his grade.
A grade of A is the best.

easy.def: To finish school and get a paper that says so.
examples: She will graduate this spring.
My brother graduated from high school.
They graduated from college.

more.def: To complete your studies at a school and receive a diploma.
examples: My sister will graduate from high school in June.
He graduated from college and became a teacher.
The whole class graduated and tossed their caps.

easy.def: A person who has finished school.
examples: She is a graduate of our school.
The graduates wore gowns.
He is a college graduate.

more.def: A person who has finished a school or course of study and gotten a diploma.
examples: The graduates tossed their caps in the air.
She is a graduate of the local high school.
He is a college graduate who became a scientist.
A grand castle.
The grand hall.
It was a grand party.

more.def: Large, impressive and fancy.
examples: The king lived in a grand castle.
They held a grand party for the whole town.
The theater has a grand staircase.

easy.def: The father of your mother or father.
examples: My grandfather tells jokes.
Grandfather fixes my bike.
I went fishing with my grandfather.

more.def: The father of one of your parents.
examples: My grandfather taught me to play chess.
Her grandfather grows tomatoes in his garden.
He built a treehouse with his grandfather.
Grandma bakes cookies.
I visit my grandma.
Grandma reads to me.

more.def: The mother of your mother or father.
examples: My grandma tells great stories.
We spent the weekend at Grandma's house.
Both of my grandmas live nearby.

easy.def: The mother of your mother or father.
examples: My grandmother tells great stories.
I visit my grandmother on Sundays.
Grandmother made me a hat.

more.def: The mother of one of your parents.
examples: My grandmother taught me how to knit a scarf.
Her grandmother lives in a small town by the sea.
He baked cookies with his grandmother for the school sale.
Grandpa fishes with me.
I visit my grandpa.
Grandpa tells jokes.

more.def: The father of your mother or father.
examples: My grandpa taught me to fish.
We spent the weekend at Grandpa's house.
Both of my grandpas live nearby.

easy.def: Green plants that grow close to the ground.
examples: The grass is green.
I lay on the grass.
The cow ate grass.

more.def: A low, green plant with thin leaves that covers lawns and fields.
examples: We sat on the soft grass in the park.
The cows chewed the grass.
Dad cut the grass on Saturday.
I am grateful for my family.
I am grateful for your help.
We are grateful for the sunny day.

more.def: Feeling or showing thanks for something good.
examples: We were grateful to the neighbors who helped us move.
The lost hikers were grateful to see the rescue team.
She wrote a note to say how grateful she was for the gift.

easy.def: A place in the ground where someone is buried.
examples: The grave is quiet.
We put flowers on the grave.
She visited her great-grandfather's grave.

more.def: A hole in the ground, or a place, where a dead person is buried.
examples: Children placed flowers at the grave.
The old graves were marked with stones.
She visited her grandfather's grave.
The news was grave.
He gave a grave look.
The doctor looked grave.

more.def: Very serious or important.
examples: The news of the storm was grave.
The captain gave a grave look.
The doctor spoke in a grave voice.

easy.def: What pulls things down to the ground.
examples: Gravity makes the ball fall down.
Gravity keeps us on the ground.
Without gravity, we would float.

more.def: The force that pulls objects toward the Earth and keeps us on the ground.
examples: Because of gravity, a dropped pencil always falls to the floor.
Gravity pulls the rain down from the clouds.
There is less gravity on the moon than on Earth.

easy.def: The color between black and white.
examples: The cloud is gray.
My cat is gray.
The elephant is gray.

more.def: Having the color between black and white, like a rain cloud.
examples: The sky was gray before the storm.
A gray squirrel ran up the tree.
Grandpa has gray hair.

easy.def: The color between black and white.
examples: Gray is a dull color.
Mix black and white to make gray.
The sky turned to gray.

more.def: The color that is made by mixing black and white.
examples: Gray is what you get when black meets white.
The artist painted the storm clouds in gray.
The sea was a flat gray.
We had a great day.
That is a great idea.
She is a great singer.

more.def: Very good, or much larger or more important than usual.
examples: Our team had a great game and won by a lot.
The Great Wall is one of the longest walls in the world.
A great storm blew across the plains.
The greedy boy took all the cookies.
Do not be greedy. Take just one.
The greedy dog ate the cat's food too.

more.def: Wanting much more of something than you need or than is fair.
examples: The greedy king kept all the gold for himself.
The greedy pirate wanted all the treasure for himself.
It would be greedy to take more than your share.
Grass is green.
A green frog sat there.
She wore a green coat.

more.def: Having the color of grass or leaves.
examples: Frogs are often green.
The green leaves danced in the wind.
He painted the fence green.
Green is my favorite color.
Mix blue and yellow to make green.
The leaves are a bright green.

more.def: The color of fresh leaves and grass.
examples: The artist used many shades of green.
Spring turns the fields to green.
Green looks bright on a sunny day.
The smell is gross.
The old milk is gross.
That is gross!

more.def: Very unpleasant or disgusting.
examples: The rotten food was gross.
The smell from the trash was gross.
That is gross, so please wash your hands.

easy.def: The earth that you walk on.
examples: The ground is wet.
Sit on the ground.
The apple fell to the ground.

more.def: The solid surface of the Earth that you stand and walk on.
examples: Snow covered the ground.
The ground shook when the truck passed.
She planted the seeds in the soft ground.
A group of kids played.
A group of ducks swam by.
We sat in a group.

more.def: A number of people, animals or things that are together.
examples: A group of students waited for the bus.
A group of whales swam past the boat.
Sort the shapes into three groups.

easy.def: To put things together in sets.
examples: Group the toys by color.
She grouped the cards.
We grouped the blocks.

more.def: To put people or things together into sets.
examples: Group the buttons by color.
The teacher grouped us in pairs.
She grouped the animals by where they live.
Plants grow in the sun.

The puppy grew bigger.

more.def: To become bigger or taller as time passes.
examples: Sunflowers can grow taller than a grown-up.
The town grew as more families moved in.
My hair has grown a lot since last spring.

easy.def: To plant something and take care of it.
examples: We grow tomatoes in our garden.
Farmers grow corn.
She grew beans in a cup.

more.def: To plant seeds or young plants and take care of them until they are ready.
examples: Grandpa grows vegetables behind his house.
Farmers in this valley grow apples and pears.
We grew sunflowers for the school fair.

easy.def: To slowly become a certain way.
examples: It grows dark early in winter.
She grew tired of waiting.
He grew sleepy in the car.

more.def: To slowly change until something is a certain way.
examples: The sky grew dark as the storm came closer.
The puppy grew sleepy after its walk.
As the music grew louder, the crowd began to clap.
I am grumpy when I am tired.
The grumpy man did not smile.
My cat is grumpy after a bath.

more.def: Easily annoyed and in a bad mood.
examples: He is always grumpy before he has eaten breakfast.
The grumpy troll would not let anyone cross the bridge.
She felt grumpy because she had slept badly.
